doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Duo records with Mottola and George Barnes
summary: His favorite records are duos, starting with Mottola, then George Barnes after he got the seven-string.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: No kidding. What a life, huh? You recorded some marvelous duo records, in fact I think you said some of your best things are duos?

Oh yeah. My favorite records are — the first duo I made was with Tony Mottola, then I got hooked up with George Barnes who is one of America’s great individual guitar players I ever heard, nobody played like George, and he was in the studio scene with us. And he was fed up with them, so he always had little projects going on with jazz on the weekend somewhere, and some little project where he arranged something that had a lot of body to it, and Jack Lesberg was involved, I was, George, and then George and I really hooked up when I got my seven string guitar. Because he had been playing duets with Carl Kress, one of my heroes.
And Zoot Sims and Stephane Grappelli, all those folks.
When you got together to do a duo record with some of those people, mostly just talking through tunes, picking out tunes, did you rehearse it a lot?
